about: The stage at the top of every demo page (tools/stage.py writes it between <!-- stage:start --> and <!-- stage:end -->). mode replace: the page's old hero became the stage. mode prepend: the stage sits above the page's old hero, whose kicker and h1 moved up into the stage panel; the rest (box builders, desks, chapter menus) stays where it was. Captions: the shop's own words where his site has them, verbatim.

how.pickup: Pickup at 169 W Green St: choose the day and the time, and it is boxed for then.
how.delivery: Delivery runs on Uber Eats, DoorDash and Grubhub today, through the shop’s menu app. Shelf gifts also ship in the US.

adopted.h1: The éclair case at 169 W Green St, made entirely from plants.
adopted.kicker: Pâtisserie françaiseSalon de thé100% plant-based
adopted.lead: Glossy chocolate, espresso and pistachio éclairs under gold leaf, croissants laminated with plant butter, macarons by the six. A fourth-generation pastry chef fills the case in Old Pasadena, and you choose the moment it is boxed for you.

adopted.h1: Today’s case at 169 W Green St, boxed for your time.
adopted.lead: Every éclair, croissant, macaron and jar, at the shop’s own prices.

adopted.h1: Custom cakes from 169 W Green St, one week ahead.
adopted.kicker: Custom cakesOne week’s notice100% plant-based
adopted.lead: Tell the chef the occasion, the guests and the flavour, and get a sketch and a price back. Give it a week’s notice.

adopted.h1: Macaron Masterclass with Chef Romy, Tuesdays at 3:30.
adopted.kicker: $125.00 a seat169 W Green St
adopted.lead: Two hands-on hours at the shop. You leave with 20 to 30 macarons.

adopted.h1: La Cave, next door at 163. Un verre, un éclair.
adopted.lead: One glass, one éclair. La Cave is the pâtisserie’s evening, one door down: organic, biodynamic and vegan wines, mostly French varietals from California and abroad, Rebel Cheese boards, and plated desserts from the kitchen next door with a glass poured to match.

adopted.h1: Romuald Guiot, fourth generation. Every pastry from plants.
adopted.lead: Chef Romy trained at La Maison de Marc Veyrat, three Michelin stars, opened La Mirabelle in New York and reached the final of Food Network’s Spring Baking Championship. At 169 W Green St he makes French pâtisserie with no animal products at all, and guests are often surprised to learn it.

adopted.h1: From Green Street, in navy and ivory.
adopted.kicker: Planned lineNavy and ivoryNo animal materials
adopted.lead: Eight pieces for the first run, each with one French line and the red heart from the logo, plus numbered macaron tins and counter pieces that change with the season. The line is planned and not for sale yet; three things can be ordered today.

adopted.h1: A table from the case at 169 W Green St, for ten or for forty.
adopted.kicker: Events and officesPickup at 169 W Green St100% vegan
adopted.lead: The board for ten, trays of macarons and cannelés, a box of jars, cookies printed with your logo. Tell the kitchen the date and the headcount; it answers with what it can make by then and a price.

adopted.h1: Give the case at 169 W Green St, and let them choose.
adopted.kicker: Gift cardsSent by email, the same minuteSpent at the counter or online
adopted.lead: A card for the éclair case, the salon de thé, a box of macarons or a seat at the masterclass. Pick an amount, write a line, and it lands in their inbox now or on the morning you choose.

adopted.h1: The board behind the counter at 169 W Green St, the same file as the website.
adopted.kicker: The counter board169 W Green StEvery price from the menu file
adopted.lead: One menu file feeds the website, the pickup app and this board, so a price changes in one place. Print it for the counter, or open it on the shop screen; it is redrawn from the menu before every publish.

adopted.h1: The vitrine at 169 W Green St, boxed for the time you choose.
adopted.kicker: Pâtisserie française and salon de thé, 100% plant-based
adopted.lead: Chef Romuald Guiot trained at three-Michelin-star La Maison de Marc Veyrat and reached the Spring Baking Championship final. Every piece in his case is made from plants. Pick a pickup slot, then fill the box from 43 pieces on six shelves.

adopted.h1: An afternoon at 169 West Green Street.
adopted.kicker: Pâtisserie française et salon de thé, 100% plant-based, in Old Pasadena
adopted.lead: French pastry by Chef Romuald Guiot, trained in a three-Michelin-star kitchen and made entirely from plants. Order from the case for the hour you choose, sit down to afternoon tea, or take a Tuesday seat at his bench.

adopted.h1: Pâtisserie française by Romuald Guiot, made from plants at 169 W Green St.
adopted.lead: A fourth-generation pastry chef, formerly of the three-Michelin-star La Maison de Marc Veyrat. Every éclair, croissant and macaron in his case is plant-based, and every one can be boxed for the 15-minute pickup slot you choose.

adopted.h1: Fill a box of 6 for $15.
adopted.lead: Boxed at 169 W Green St in Old Pasadena for the time you choose, and made from plants, like everything in the case.

adopted.h1: The whole counter at 169 W Green St, in three taps.
adopted.lead: Add what you want, open the bag, pay. Éclairs from $5.50, six macarons for $15.00, all of it plant-based.

adopted.h1: The house of the éclair, at 169 W Green St.
adopted.kicker: Pâtisserie française · Salon de thé · 100% plant-based
adopted.lead: French pâtisserie by Chef Romuald Guiot, trained at the three-Michelin-star La Maison de Marc Veyrat and made entirely from plants. Gifts boxed by the house; the case ready at the hour you choose.

adopted.h1: One day at 169 W Green St, from the 6 am case to La Cave at 9.
adopted.kicker: Pâtisserie française and salon de thé · 100% plant-based · Old Pasadena
adopted.lead: Chef Romuald Guiot trained at the three-Michelin-star La Maison de Marc Veyrat and makes every pastry here from plants. Scroll through his day: the vitrine, a box chosen for you in three questions, pickup in two taps, tea and the Tuesday masterclass at half past three, then a glass next door.

adopted.h1: Ask the counter at 169 W Green St. It answers from the menu.
adopted.lead: Prices, gluten-free marks, a cake’s notice, Tuesday’s $125.00 class, La Cave’s hours: ask, and Le Concierge answers from the shop’s own menu, shows where each answer came from and puts what you choose in the bag. What you type stays on this page.
